osmTags.inscription: The Townhouse, 1825: A police office and jail on the ground floor and a court-room on the first. It served as a cholera hospital, a barracks and in 1854 it was Scotland's first free library.
New Cross Airdrie, road dates from 1795.

Foundation Stone.
Laid - 5th Mar 1957
Opened - 23rd Mar 1959

Jean Weir, great-grand-daughter of Robert Burns baptised here on 21st March 1841.
— Airdrie Burns Club inst. 1884

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.

notes: site: no closed historic=* way/relation found; location-only scene
present-day buildings capped: kept the 120 nearest the outline centre of 128 mapped (trace size budget); the rest of the town is not drawn
roads capped: kept the 150 longest of 205 mapped (trace size budget); minor lanes are not drawn
